| [NOTE-1437](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1437.md) | Moreno & Mossio — Biological Autonomy, the Introduction | The Introduction alone. Moreno and Mossio state their programme: the organism, not natural selection, is biology's central idea; its core is a closure of constraints, which they say fundamentally differs from the process loops and self-organisation of dissipative structures, and which grounds teleology, normativity and function. With regulation and agency, closure makes an autonomous system, an organism; ecosystems meet only closure. The arguments are announced for chapters 1–7, which this reading does not cover. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1440](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1440.md) | Rung & Madden — Experimental reductions of delay discounting | A systematic review and category-wise meta-analysis of 92 papers that tried to lower delay discounting without drugs or lesions. Most kinds of manipulation worked, learning-based ones such as bundling and delay fading best. Clinical interventions moved discounting little, and mindfulness and ACT, two studies, only at trend level (g = 0.32, p = .06). Mediation was almost never tested, so how any manipulation lowers discounting is unknown. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1454.md) | Flynn, Kanerva & Bhadkamkar — SDM principles and operation | Kanerva and co-authors state SDM's critical distance in words and do not derive it: a cue within it converges on the stored pattern under iterated reads, a cue beyond it wanders and may settle on another pattern, the distance shrinks as the memory fills, and in a sparsely filled memory it is below the sum of the write and read radii. For single patterns convergence and divergence are "easy to distinguish in practice"; for stored sequences they are not. The rest of the report is a hardware design. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1472](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1472.md) | Falasco & Esposito — macroscopic stochastic thermodynamics | Builds macroscopic stochastic thermodynamics from Markov jump processes with local detailed balance. Under extensive rates and potentials, a deterministic dynamics emerges whose Lyapunov function is the quasi-potential I_ss, and a large-deviation theory of fluctuations around it. Transition rates between attractors go as e^{−VΔI_ss} and are bracketed by the entropy produced along relaxation and escape paths; the bracket closes only near detailed balance. Gaussian-noise Langevin equations mis-estimate both the barriers and the entropy production. Read for those parts and the Schlögl example; field theory and two of three applications not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1486](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1486.md) | Massumi — The Principle of Unrest | Interviews and an essay in activist philosophy. Movement is qualitative relational transformation, and capitalism an ontopower feeding on "bare activity". Micropolitics aims at "a maximally inclusive co-patterning of contrasting tendencies" (p. 64), an aesthetic ideal that affirms discord rather than resolving it. The parent paper's quotation is exact; it turns the ideal into a description of organizational becoming. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1499](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1499.md) | Metzinger — The Elephant and the Blind | More than 500 meditators' retrospective reports of "pure awareness", from a survey of 1,403 people in 57 countries, are offered as evidence that consciousness occurs without time, self-location, an egoic self-model or a first-person perspective. Pure awareness is modelled as the top level of a nested active-inference hierarchy, "a highest-level but nonegoic self-model" of the organism's own epistemic openness. The book concedes that retrospective reports cannot show that a state was selfless when it happened, and its summary calls nonegoic consciousness "empirically established" all the same. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1504](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1504.md) | Heymann & Vanden-Eijnden — The geometric minimum action method | The Freidlin–Wentzell quasi-potential, a double minimization over paths and their duration, is rewritten as a single minimization over curves of a parametrization-free action, which has minimizers when the end points are equilibria and is computed by a string-method-like relaxation (gMAM). For a diffusion it is V = 2 inf ∫ \|b\| sin²(θ/2) ds. In gradient systems with identity noise the most likely transition paths are parallel to the drift; in the nongradient Maier–Stein model they depart from the heteroclinic orbit once the drift is far enough from gradient. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1535](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1535.md) | Bishop — Chaos (SEP) | The 2024 revision of Bishop's SEP entry. Chaos is a property of deterministic models; unpredictability is not indeterminism. The sensitive-dependence argument that chaos amplifies quantum events is qualified: damping, negative local Lyapunov exponents and, in the brain, "parallel redundancy" may stop amplification. For Kane, sensitivity alone does not give incompatibilist freedom, and the incompatibilist must still show agents can "harness" indeterminism. §6.2–6.3 state Bishop's contextual emergence as an ontological account: larger-scale stability conditions that constrain and enable smaller-scale behaviour. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1536](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1536.md) | Scheffer et al. — Early-warning signals for critical transitions | A review of generic early-warning signals for critical transitions. At a fold bifurcation the dominant eigenvalue goes to zero, so recovery from small perturbations slows (critical slowing down). Under ongoing perturbation that shows as rising lag-1 autocorrelation and rising variance. Skewness and flickering are further signals, not caused by slowing down. Spatial systems add rising cross-correlation and specific pattern sequences. Evidence from climate, ecosystems, epilepsy, asthma and finance is reviewed. The signals mark proximity to a broad class of thresholds, not only catastrophic ones, so they do not say which kind; false positives and negatives are named. Cyclic and chaotic systems are "less well studied". | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1539](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1539.md) | Crowell, Beauchaine and Linehan — A biosocial developmental model of borderline personality | Linehan's biosocial theory as restated with her: emotion dysregulation, "heightened emotional sensitivity", inability to regulate intense responses and "slow return to emotional baseline", is the core, and cognitive dysregulation is among its consequences, "distorted information processing" and difficulty organizing toward "non-mood-dependent goals". Skimmed; read for the theory, not the biology. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1555](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1555.md) v2 | Zhuk — A proof of the CSP dichotomy conjecture | Zhuk proves the CSP dichotomy for finite domains independently of Bulatov: for a finite language Γ on a finite set, CSP(Γ) is in P if a weak near-unanimity operation preserves Γ, NP-complete otherwise. The algorithm checks local consistency, reduces domains to absorbing subuniverses, centres or quotients, and in the linear case solves linear equations over prime fields. Read: the introduction, outline, definitions, the structural Theorem 5.1 with proof, and the conclusions; the main proofs not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1562](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1562.md) | Freidlin & Wentzell — Random Perturbations of Dynamical Systems, front matter | Front matter only. The Introduction outlines the programme: limit theorems for small random perturbations of a dynamical system, of which the rough large-deviation results matter most, because the probabilities of rare events on finite intervals decide behaviour on infinite ones. An action functional S(ϕ) gives P{ρ(Xᵋ, ϕ) < δ} ≈ exp{−ε⁻²S(ϕ)}; the exit time from a domain is approximately exponential, and with several stable sets the stationary distribution concentrates on the one with the larger infimum of S for leaving it. The theorems themselves are in chapters not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1572](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1572.md) v2 | Bulatov — A dichotomy theorem for nonuniform CSPs | Bulatov proves the CSP dichotomy for finite domains: every CSP(Γ) over a finite constraint language on a finite set is in P or NP-complete, P exactly when the polymorphisms include a weak near-unanimity operation. The new part is the algorithm, which combines local consistency, a new non-local condition (block-minimality) and the few-subpowers algorithm. Read: the introduction and §§2–3.2's opening; the ~80 pages of proof were not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1658.md) v2 | Mauss — Essai sur le don | Mauss's comparative essay on the gift, skimmed with its introduction, first chapter, the Northwest-coast section and its conclusion read in full. Gifts in archaic societies are voluntary in form and obligatory in fact, between collectivities, under three obligations: to give, to receive and to return. The Maori hau of the thing given seeks its origin; the potlatch is returned with interest on pain of lost face, rank and freedom. To accept without returning is to become client and servant. The conclusion carries this into modern morality: charity wounds, social insurance is a return owed to the worker, and the individual must still rely on himself. Interpretive, on second-hand ethnography. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1680](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1680.md) v2 | LaVoice — Slum clearance and the neighbourhoods cleared, read from a short draft | About 200 Title I projects funded before 1965 in 28 large US cities, geocoded to census tracts for 1940–2000. Among similarly blighted tracts, black neighbourhoods were two to three times as likely to be cleared. Against slums in cities with limited participation, cleared tracts kept about 13% lower population density, 12% lower housing density and a 16% lower black share for decades, with rents up about a quarter and incomes up for a decade and then fading; the draft gives the income gain as 18% and as 16% without reconciling them. Within cities, rents in untreated low-income tracts rose in step, and a spatial-equilibrium model reads the lowest-income households city-wide as made worse off. The displaced are not tracked and social ties are not measured. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1716.md) | Kiczales, Lamping, Mendhekar, Maeda, Lopes, Loingtier and Irwin — Aspect-oriented programming | Aspect-oriented programming, by the metaobject-protocol book's first author and his group. Read for its one paragraph on reflection and metaobject protocols, and its decision to bound raw reflective access with a narrower language. A weak stand-in for Part I of The Art of the Metaobject Protocol. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1718](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1718.md) | Kiczales, des Rivières and Bobrow — The Art of the Metaobject Protocol, chapter 5 | Chapter 5 specifies a metaobject protocol for CLOS: the language described as an extensible program whose classes, generic functions, methods and method combinations are metaobjects users may specialize, within stated restrictions on users and implementors, with redefinition propagated to dependents. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1733](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1733.md) | Greely (2026) — Alabama's LePage decision, the future of ex vivo embryos, and more | Greely revisits his 2022 prediction that IVF would survive Dobbs. In LePage v. Center for Reproductive Medicine (16 Feb 2024) the Alabama Supreme Court held frozen embryos to be "minor children" under the 1872 Wrongful Death of a Minor Act. Greely argues the holding was narrow: it extended one cause of action, and in Alabama wrongful death allows only punitive damages, which is why the plaintiffs, IVF parents who wanted more children, needed it. It would not have ended IVF (Louisiana has barred destroying viable embryos since 1986 and still has clinics). The language of the majority and Chief Justice Parker's theological concurrence provoked media and political overreaction; within 19 days the legislature gave IVF clinics and suppliers broad civil and criminal immunity, which Greely thinks far too broad, since negligent destruction of embryos (e.g. the 2018 Cleveland and San Francisco tank failures) should carry liability. He concludes IVF remains largely safe because its political support is broad, and draws lessons on state-law diversity, media coverage of nuanced decisions and judicial language. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1736](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1736.md) | Dierickx and others (2024) — A data-centric approach for ethical and trustworthy AI in journalism | Proposes the Accuracy-Fairness-Transparency (AFT) framework for assessing the quality of datasets used to build machine-learning tools in newsrooms, deriving data-quality checks from three core principles of journalism ethics, and placing the work in the shift from model-centric to data-centric AI. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1738.md) | Nakhal et al. (2026) — Maternal gut dysbiosis is associated with altered enteric and cortical inhibitory circuit development | Pregnant GAD67-GFP mice (6 control, 6 treated dams) received oral vancomycin (20 mg/kg/day, GD8–GD17) to induce gut dysbiosis. Dams' microbiota lost diversity (Chao1, Shannon; PERMANOVA R² = 0.77). In offspring at postnatal day 14 (12 pups per group), the authors report lower maternal–offspring microbial transmission fidelity, reduced body weight, crypt and muscularis thickness, fragmented Claudin-1, reduced myenteric (Auerbach's) plexus area without change in neuronal density, shorter and less branched GAD67+ interneurons in layers II/III of somatosensory and motor cortex (not medial entorhinal cortex or CA1), and lower interneuron density in motor cortex only. Correlations between offspring taxa and these phenotypes are reported. The authors repeatedly label the findings descriptive associations. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1739.md) | Stand-in reading — Monnier, George, Guyard, Tarnec & Kountouris — MIFair: A Mutual-Information Framework for Intersectionality and Multiclass Fairness | A mutual-information-based template for fairness metrics and an in-processing mitigation (a regularizer inspired by the Prejudice Remover), covering independence- and separation-based notions, intersectional sensitive attributes and multiclass outputs, tested on tabular and image data. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1746.md) | Caliari and Petri — Irrational Random Utility Models | The random utility model (RUM) treats aggregate stochastic choice as generated by a population of preference maximizers. The authors show that RUM data can equally be generated by a population of decision-makers none of whom maximizes a preference, if and only if the rational population's preferences are "sufficiently uncorrelated" (their correlation bounds, a strengthening of lower Fréchet bounds). Consequences: the rational interpretation of RUMs is hard to falsify; individual rationality cannot be inferred from aggregate data without prior knowledge; welfare conclusions depend on which representation the analyst adopts. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1747](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1747.md) | Amano and Simonov (working paper) — What Makes Players Pay? An Empirical Investigation of In-Game Lotteries | Using the complete action and transaction log of one free-to-play mobile puzzle game (2.5 million users, about 20 million paid loot boxes, 96% of in-game revenue from loot boxes), the authors estimate a dynamic discrete-choice model in which loot boxes can have "functional" value (better items raise win probability) and "direct" value (utility from opening, plus state dependence). Estimating separately for "whales" (top spenders) and others, they find regular players value loot boxes mostly for gameplay and whales mostly for the direct utility. Simulations evaluate a loot-box ban, a paid-loot-box ban, spending caps and changes in game difficulty. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1750](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1750.md) | Næss (working paper) — Investigative journalism: Market failures and government intervention through public broadcasters | A public-goods model plus survey experiments. Each person's payoff from investigative journalism is shared; a firm selling access can collect only private willingness to pay (WTP), so when marginal cost lies between one person's marginal benefit and the sum over N people, provision is Pareto-inefficiently low. Surveys measure WTP for three days of investigative journalism and support for funding it through public broadcasters versus subsidies to private media; treatments test exclusive access (a Coasian property-rights fix), widespread dissemination, and a promise of political neutrality. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1754](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1754.md) | Digital Services Act — Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 on a Single Market For Digital Services (Digital Services Act) | Article 25(1) forbids online platforms to "design, organise or operate their online interfaces in a way that deceives or manipulates the recipients of their service or in a way that otherwise materially distorts or impairs the ability of the recipients of their service to make free and informed decisions". Article 25(2) excludes practices already covered by the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive (2005/29/EC) or the GDPR, and 25(3) lets the Commission issue guidance on prominence of choices, repeated prompts and cancellation harder than sign-up. Article 27 requires platforms using recommender systems to state the "main parameters" in their terms, explain "why certain information is suggested", and offer any available options for changing them. Article 38 requires very large platforms and search engines to provide "at least one option for each of their recommender systems which is not based on profiling". Recital 67 defines dark patterns as practices that "materially distort or impair, either on purpose or in effect", the ability to make "autonomous and informed choices". | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1755](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1755.md) | Muñoz et al. (2020) — Researcher Perspectives on Ethical Considerations in Adaptive Deep Brain Stimulation Trials | Semi-structured interviews with 23 researchers in aDBS trials, thematic analysis. Eight themes, by frequency: data privacy and security (91%), risks and safety (83%), informed consent (74%), automaticity and device programming (65%), patient autonomy and control over stimulation (57%), patient selection (39%), post-trial access (39%), personality and identity (30%). | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1756.md) | Cuny and Poelman (2022) — Evolution of koinobiont parasitoid host regulation and consequences for indirect plant defence | Koinobiont parasitoids let the host keep feeding while their larvae develop inside it, and regulate the host's growth: usually arresting it (smaller hosts eating less), sometimes prolonging it (larger hosts eating more), and some species switch with conditions. The regulation is done by injected and secreted factors, and it changes the plant's responses to the parasitized herbivore, so it reaches the wider community. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1757](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1757.md) | Liang and others (2024) — Monitoring AI-Modified Content at Scale: A Case Study on the Impact of ChatGPT on AI Conference Peer Reviews | The authors estimate, at corpus level, the fraction α of text substantially modified or generated by an LLM, by maximum likelihood over word-frequency distributions estimated from human-written and AI-generated reference corpora, validated on semi-synthetic mixtures. Applied to peer reviews, α rose sharply after ChatGPT's release at ML conferences (ICLR 1.6% to 10.6%; NeurIPS 1.9% to 9.1%; CoRL 2.4% to 6.5%; EMNLP about 16.9%) but not in Nature-portfolio reviews. Estimated LLM use is higher for reviews submitted within three days of the deadline, without scholarly citations, from reviewers who do not reply to rebuttals, with low self-rated confidence, and in reviews closest to the centroid of a paper's reviews (homogenization). | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1758.md) | Jia and others 2026 — Neuron–tumor crosstalk in cancer: molecular mechanisms and translational advances | A narrative review of cancer neuroscience. Tumours recruit nerves (neurotrophins such as NGF and BDNF, axon-guidance cues, perineural invasion) or, in the brain, integrate into existing circuits through tumour–neuron synapses; nerve signalling, chiefly sympathetic norepinephrine through β-adrenergic receptors, then builds an immunosuppressive microenvironment; nerves also reach the tumour through endocrine and metabolic routes, including the transfer of mitochondria from neurons to cancer cells; and cancer pain feeds a loop that raises sympathetic tone. The authors name the whole pattern "tumor neuron hijack" and propose repurposed β-blockers, cholinergic drugs and neural-signal modulation, especially with immunotherapy. It reports no new data; most mechanisms it cites are preclinical. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1761](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1761.md) | Gao, Lee and Murphy (2018 working paper) — Financing dies in darkness? The impact of newspaper closures on public finance | Using U.S. daily newspaper data (1996–2015; 1,596 newspapers in 1,266 counties; 296 exits) and municipal bond data (MSRB, 1999–2015), the authors study the long-run effect of local newspaper closures on municipal borrowing costs. Focusing on closures that leave a county with two or fewer dailies (204 "Closure" counties), they find offering yields rise by about 5.5 bp and secondary yields by 6.4 bp three or more years after a closure, more for revenue bonds (about 10 bp), costing about $650 thousand per average issue. Identification: comparison with population-matched neighbouring counties (7.3 bp); closures in low- vs high-newspaper counties (10.3 bp vs no effect); Craigslist entry as an instrument for closures (4–6 bp). Effects are larger in states with isolated capitals (worse governance) and do not differ by internet use (online news not a substitute). Mechanisms: government inefficiency (more costly advance refundings and negotiated sales; higher government wage share, employees per capita, taxes and deficits per capita) and informational frictions (price dispersion up about 5%). | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1767.md) | Ahmed and others (2022) — Microbiota-derived metabolites as drivers of gut–brain communication | A review of how gut-microbial metabolites (SCFAs, tryptophan/indole derivatives, bile acids, sulfated phenolics and others) influence brain functions through immune, neural and endocrine routes, arranged by neurological function, with a closing assessment of how far human evidence supports the preclinical picture. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1768](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1768.md) | Chua et al. — Key questions and challenges in microchimerism biology | An expert survey (29 researchers, 63 unique questions in seven themes) that states the field's settled points and open questions. Microchimeric cells are rare, persist for decades, cross into almost any tissue, and are tolerated partly by actively induced regulatory T cells; the depletion of one marked maternal subset removes tolerance without lowering total microchimerism. What they do, why they persist, and what counts as microchimerism are open. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1772](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1772.md) | George and Bates (2022) — Mechanisms Underlying Influence of Bioelectricity in Development | A review of how ion channels and membrane potential (Vmem) act in development: human channelopathies with developmental phenotypes, conserved roles across species, spontaneous calcium oscillations in non-excitable tissue, and the cellular processes (death, proliferation, polarity, migration) and signalling pathways (BMP, Notch, Wnt, Hedgehog) that channels touch. It proposes calcium as the main mediator and a model in which Vmem and calcium oscillations, shaped by mechanical forces, coordinate cells across a tissue. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1773](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1773.md) | Almarzooqi and others (2026) — From association to causality: mechanistic pathways linking the gut microbiome to psychiatric disorders | A narrative review of the microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA) in psychiatry, organized around the move "from association to causality". It sets out a graded hierarchy of causal evidence (confounder-controlled association, temporal precedence, experimental necessity/sufficiency, human genetic or interventional validation, cross-cohort replication), reviews mechanisms (immune, HPA, vagal/ENS, barrier), grades the evidence per disorder, and reviews translation (psychobiotics, diet, FMT, biomarkers). Its verdict: the microbiome is "a biologically plausible and modifiable contributor within a complex, bidirectional system rather than a primary cause"; MDD has "moderate causal involvement"; anxiety and BD weaker; SCZ a disease modifier. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1778](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1778.md) | Gan (2022) — Gacha Game: When Prospect Theory Meets Optimal Pricing | A seller sells one good to a buyer with cumulative prospect theory preferences whose value is known. Probability weighting makes the buyer dynamically inconsistent. If she is naive, the unique optimum is a stationary loot box (a constant chance of the good per paid period); if sophisticated, the optimum adds worst-case insurance: after enough failures she can buy the good outright, which resembles the "pity system" of gacha games. With payments restricted to be non-negative (no paying the buyer), profit is bounded; with negative prices allowed, as in gambling, it is not, which Gan offers as a theoretical line between loot boxes and gambling and a reason to watch resale markets. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1785](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1785.md) | Mpakosi and others (2024) — Deciphering the Role of Maternal Microchimerism in Offspring Autoimmunity: A Narrative Review | A narrative review of maternal-to-offspring microchimerism (MMc). Cells cross the placenta both ways; maternal cells enter the fetus from the second trimester and persist into adulthood. They include T cells, B and NK cells, monocytes and haematopoietic and mesenchymal progenitors; levels depend on HLA compatibility, PAPP-A and possibly delivery mode; MMc may pass across generations (grandmother, siblings). Protective roles: immune maturation, early-life infection defence, possibly transfer of pathogen-specific T-cell memory, tolerance to non-inherited maternal antigens via MSCs. Harmful associations: type 1 diabetes, neonatal lupus, juvenile myopathies, Sjögren's and others (no association with coeliac disease). The authors conclude the role remains unclear and the evidence is hampered by detection limits, small samples and non-standard methods. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1786](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1786.md) | Brenninger, Zug & Kokko (2025) — Infection dynamics of endosymbionts that manipulate arthropod reproduction | A unified minimal model of the infection dynamics of maternally transmitted endosymbionts (Wolbachia, Rickettsia, Cardinium, Spiroplasma and others) that manipulate arthropod reproduction: male-killing, feminization, parthenogenesis induction, sex-allocation distortion and cytoplasmic incompatibility (CI), in diplodiploid and haplodiploid hosts. It gives invasion criteria for single strains and for pairs of manipulators. CI's positive frequency dependence makes it hard to invade from rarity but hard to displace once established (a priority effect), which may explain why it is the most common in nature. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1788.md) | Harman, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 2025 — The Ethics of Abortion | The entry asks one question: "is abortion morally wrong?" It sets aside whether abortion should be legally restricted as "an open and further question". It is organised as six arguments against abortion (from a right to life, from loss, from the Golden Rule, from intrinsic value, from moral risk, and the expressive argument against selective abortion). Each is followed by subsections presenting replies, and a seventh part says why the question matters. In the sections read: - §1 sets out the right-to-life argument as a numbered syllogism. - §1.2 presents Thomson's violinist case. It "defends abortion while granting the claim that the fetus has a right to life", by targeting the premise that it is wrong to kill anything that has a right to life. - §1.2.1 considers the reply from consensual sex and answers it with a variant of the case. - §1.2.2 asks whether the violinist case gives a positive argument for permissibility. - §1.4 asks whether potential to become a right-holder is enough to have a right to life now. - §2.2 rejects the claim that the fetus is deprived of a valuable future. It appeals to the psychological connections that ordinary persons bear to their futures (McInerney), and to McMahan's time-relative interests view, on which the pre-conscious fetus "has no interest in any of its valuable future". - §2.3 argues that the argument from loss and the violinist argument do not conflict: the second grants what the first concludes. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1790](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1790.md) | UNESCO General Conference (2025) — Recommendation on the Ethics of Neurotechnology | A human-rights-based instrument covering neurotechnology's whole life cycle, medical and non-medical, and extending to "indirect neural data and non-neural data allowing mental states inferences". Core principles include autonomy (individual and relational) and freedom of thought, protection against manipulation, mental privacy, prior free and informed consent, and specific policy measures for data, employment, consumer products, recommender systems, nudging, sleep marketing, neuromarketing and closed-loop environments. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1793](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1793.md) | Burke and others (2025) — De-centering the (Traditional) user: Multistakeholder evaluation of recommender systems | A position-and-guidance article. Recommender evaluation has been almost wholly about the end user; a multistakeholder evaluation assesses "the quality of recommendations ... across multiple groups of stakeholders". It types stakeholders (consumers, item providers, upstream, downstream, system, third-party), argues that values drive goals and goals drive metrics (value-sensitive design), and surveys ways to compare systems scored on many metrics: weighted aggregation, conversion of metrics to constraints, Pareto-frontier distance, or learning an ordering from expert pairwise judgments. It lists challenges (application and context specificity, data access, institutional reluctance, adversarial providers) and closes on governance. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1799](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1799.md) | Brussels Collaboration on Bodily Integrity (2024) — Genital Modifications in Prepubescent Minors: When May Clinicians Ethically Proceed? | Restricting itself to nonvoluntary genital cutting or surgery by licensed clinicians on prepubescent children in Global North healthcare systems, and taking no position on criminal law or religious practice outside healthcare, the collaboration argues: there is a near-universal consensus that clinicians may not perform any medically unnecessary genital procedure on endosex girls, however minimal; the sound reasons for that consensus are not benefit–risk calculations but respect for privacy, bodily integrity, developing sexual boundaries and future genital autonomy; those reasons apply equally to intersex children and endosex boys; so clinicians should perform no nonvoluntary genital cutting or surgery on any child unless it is medically necessary in a strict sense (a serious, time-sensitive threat to physical health, no less invasive or postponable alternative, preserving future choice). They reject the "mental health" defence of early surgery, hold that errors of commission and omission are not symmetric, and invoke Feinberg's "right in trust". | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1825](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1825.md) | Georgiev, Gómez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner — Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale | AlphaEvolve is an evolutionary coding agent: an LLM mutates programs, a user-supplied evaluator scores them, and better programs seed the next generation. The authors apply it to 67 problems in analysis, combinatorics, geometry and number theory, mostly evolving search heuristics rather than constructions directly ("search mode"). It rediscovers the best known constructions in most cases and improves several; some findings generalize to formulas, and one (finite-field Kakeya) was proved by Deep Think and formalized in Lean by AlphaProof. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1827.md) | Leitgeb and Carus — Rudolf Carnap | The entry presents Carnap's philosophy as "conceptual engineering": philosophical problems are largely artifacts of inherited language, and the philosopher's task is to design better concepts (explication) and whole language frameworks, choosing among them for purposes rather than for truth. Frameworks fix logical (and, later, inductive) consequence; truth and existence questions are internal to a framework, while choosing a framework is a practical question. From 1932 Carnap was a pluralist ("principle of tolerance"). | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1842](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1842.md) | Polski and Ostrom — An Institutional Framework for Policy Analysis and Design | The chapter presents the Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) framework as a tool for policy analysts. The analysis proceeds in steps: - Define the policy problem and the analysis's objectives. - Analyse the physical and material conditions, the community attributes and the rules-in-use. - Integrate the analysis around the action arena: the action situation and its actors. - Evaluate patterns of interaction and outcomes. **Institutions** are "widely understood" rules, norms or strategies. **Rules-in-use** come in seven types, each matched to an element of the action situation: 1. position 2. boundary 3. authority 4. aggregation 5. scope 6. information 7. payoff **Levels of rules.** For policy systems, rules are nested at three levels: - operating (or operational) rules govern day-to-day choices; - collective-choice rules govern who may change operating rules, and how; - constitutional rules govern who may craft collective-choice rules, and how. The worked example is US interstate bank branching before and after 1994. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1848](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1848.md) | Bencomo, Götz and Song — Models@run.time: a guided tour of the state of the art and research challenges | A systematic literature review of 271 papers on models@run.time, mainly since 2006, plus 5 predecessor papers. It defines a runtime model, citing the 2009 Blair et al. article as [40], and grounds the idea in Maes's computational reflection. It builds a taxonomy: applied against fundamental research; for applied work, level of abstraction, model type, purpose and MDE technique; then domain, intersecting areas and initiatives. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1854](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1854.md) | Flouris et al. — Ontology change: classification and survey | A survey that defines "ontology change" broadly (deciding modifications in response to a need, implementing them, and managing their effects on dependent data, services and ontologies) and classifies ten subfields: mapping, morphism, matching (alignment), articulation, translation (heterogeneity resolution); evolution and debugging (modifying an ontology); versioning; integration and merging. Table 1 gives each subfield's purpose, input, output and properties. For evolution it reports Stojanovic et al. (2002)'s cyclic six-phase process (change capturing, representation, semantics of change, implementation, propagation, validation), elementary vs. composite changes, evolution strategies for side-effects, and belief-change (AGM) approaches to the semantics of change. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1859](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1859.md) | Lebo, Sahoo and McGuinness (eds.) — PROV-O: The PROV Ontology | PROV-O is the OWL2 encoding of the PROV Data Model: classes and properties to represent and interchange provenance, i.e. which entities were generated, used, derived, revised, quoted or invalidated by which activities, and which agents were responsible (attribution, association, delegation). Terms come in three tiers: Starting Point (Entity, Activity, Agent, wasGeneratedBy, used, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, ...), Expanded (Bundle, Plan, Person, wasRevisionOf, wasQuotedFrom, hadPrimarySource, wasInvalidatedBy, ...) and Qualified terms, which reify a binary influence so further attributes (role, plan, time) can be attached. It is designed to be specialized for domain provenance ontologies. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1860](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1860.md) | Mo, Zheng et al. — AgentIdeaBench: Benchmarking Scientific Ideation in the Agent Era | A benchmark for LLM scientific ideation under two matched settings: Static (the model reads a curated set of reference papers and writes one 80–150-word hypothesis) and Active (the model gets only the subfield name and a Semantic Scholar search tool with a 10-call budget, and must find its own evidence). Hypotheses are scored by an ensemble of LLM critics on originality, feasibility, clarity, impact and specificity, with originality argued against prior art retrieved at judging time. Across 33 matched models and 40 densely scored subfields in five disciplines, Active evaluation separates models more than Static, improves about twice as fast across model generations, and its gain is capability-gated; the gain comes from grounding (feasibility, clarity, specificity) and leaves measured originality unchanged. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1864](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1864.md) | Liu, Yang et al. — ResearchBench: Benchmarking LLMs in Scientific Discovery via Inspiration-Based Task Decomposition | ResearchBench evaluates LLMs on three sub-tasks into which Yang et al. (2025b) decompose hypothesis discovery: retrieving "inspirations" (papers not known to be related to the research question), composing hypotheses from background plus inspirations, and ranking hypotheses. The decomposition is claimed "sufficient": solving the sub-tasks perfectly solves discovery, under the assumption that most hypotheses arise from a background plus inspirations. An LLM agent extracts question, background, inspirations and hypothesis from 1,386 papers (2024 onward, 12 disciplines). | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1870](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1870.md) | Bragg et al. — AstaBench: Rigorous Benchmarking of AI Agents with a Scientific Research Suite | The paper argues that existing agent benchmark suites lack standard reproducible tools, ignore confounders (cost, tool access), lack standard task interfaces for general agents, lack tasks drawn from real product use, and lack comprehensive baselines. It sets out five principles and builds AstaBench to meet them: 11 benchmarks and 2,400+ problems in four categories, namely literature understanding, code and execution, data analysis, and end-to-end discovery. Alongside come a reproducible literature-search environment with date cut-offs (Asta Scientific Corpus), a cost-accounting toolkit and leaderboard (agent-eval), and an agent-baselines suite. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1871.md) | Zhang et al. — Hyperagents | The Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM) improves a coding agent by having it edit its own code, but the step that generates self-improvement instructions is fixed, and the DGM only improves at improving because task skill and self-modification skill coincide in coding. A *hyperagent* puts the task agent and the meta agent (which modifies agents) in one editable program, so the improvement procedure is itself editable ("metacognitive self-modification"). DGM-H keeps DGM's archive and open-ended exploration. | Skimmed |

Real-world tasks are scored by practical utility (accuracy of predictions made from the hypotheses, in and out of distribution) plus LLM-rated novelty, plausibility and clarity; synthetic tasks, whose generating rules are known, are scored by hypothesis discovery rate (HDR). | [NOTE-1887](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1887.md) | Park et al. — Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior | The paper builds LLM-driven agents that simulate believable everyday human behaviour in a Sims-like town of 25 agents. Its architecture has three parts: a memory stream (a timestamped list of natural-language observations), retrieval scored by recency, importance (LLM-rated poignancy) and relevance (embedding similarity), and reflection, in which the agent periodically asks itself high-level questions, retrieves memories and writes "insights" that cite the memories they came from; reflections go back into the stream and can be reflected on, forming trees.
